name: IL-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +19 partisan lean
Incumbent Mike Quigley running with a large cash advantage
Republican challenger Tommy Hanson has shown no fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price the Democrat near 96%
model.rationale: Quigley holds a +19 Democratic seat, has over $1.1 million on hand, and faces a challenger with no visible fundraising, while markets price the race at roughly 96% Democratic. Nothing in the evidence suggests movement away from the fundamentals-based Safe D call.
model.watch: Any unexpected polling showing Hanson within single digits, or major outside spending on his behalf, would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mike Quigley, a well-funded Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Chicago-area district that leans Democratic by about 19 points. He has raised over $725,000 and holds more than $1.1 million in cash, while Republican Tommy Hanson reports no fundraising and no outside support on either side. No expert raters flag the race as competitive, and prediction markets price the Democrat at roughly 96%.

With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's strong partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided financial picture. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with Quigley favored by roughly 25 points.
